task: SHELFCHECK -- CURATION DISCOVERY PASS #1 (analysis-only, no runtime/UI/census changes)
purpose: Identify categories with essentially no practical collecting/play value for Josh, while preserving weird/obscure/interesting games, per the 4 principles + horse-game callout in the task prompt. This is a discovery sample, not a full 2,536-title review, and NOT an exclusion decision -- everything here needs Josh's sign-off before any runtime change.
methodology: Loaded the real finalized runtime census (2,536 INCLUDED identities, same deterministic vm-replay harness used throughout this engagement) joined with the real shelfcheck-dossiers.txt data (1,491 dossier records). Ran keyword scans against census titles for each principle's likely vocabulary (simulator/sim, horse/pony/equestrian/ranch, kids-IP franchise names, party/sing/trivia, life/tycoon/youtuber), then individually assessed each hit's dossier text and/or general/verified knowledge. For the most consequential or ambiguous candidates (all 3 language-barrier candidates, the named Principle 2-4 examples, and several representative borderline titles), performed live web verification (English-language-support confirmation, review-aggregator gameplay-depth evidence) rather than inferring from title/region/genre alone, per Principle 1's explicit 'verify it' instruction and the general 'reason not merely genre/title/region' requirement. Separately ran a mechanical local-text scan across all 1,491 loaded dossier summaries for known wrong-content contamination patterns (Wikipedia list/disambiguation-page text, publisher/developer company bios) -- this is NOT part of the curation-judgment identity count below since it required no individual research, only string inspection of already-loaded data.

keep.whyKeep: Verified via multiple reviews: 30 songs x 2 modes = 60 levels, 4-player local co-op, 100+ collectibles, reviewers 'pleasantly surprised by the quality and amount of content.' Real design effort, not a shovelware cash-in.

projectedIncludedIfAllCutCandidatesExclu.note: Purely arithmetic projection (2536 minus 16, then minus 6 more) for planning purposes only -- no census change was made in this pass.

categoriesTooRiskyToAutomate: LOW_VALUE_ACTIVITY (party/music/trivia games) -- quality varies enormously within the category by production budget alone (The Jackbox Party Pack and Rabbids: Party of Legends vs. Party Arcade and Garfield Lasagna Party are all 'party games' but polar opposites in value). A genre/keyword rule would catch good titles.

VERY_YOUNG_LICENSED -- quality depends entirely on the specific developer/publisher, not the IP or target age. The same 'kids' license' pattern produced both a near-zero-depth title (PAW Patrol: On a Roll) and a genuinely well-made one (Bluey's Quest for the Gold Pen) from different developers. Cannot be automated by franchise or ESRB rating.

GENERIC_SIM -- the word 'Simulator' in the title has almost no correlation with quality; some of the most beloved, distinctive titles in the whole census use it ironically (Goat Simulator, Surgeon Simulator, Deeeer Simulator). A title-keyword rule would remove exactly the weirdness this pass is supposed to protect.

LANGUAGE_BARRIER is comparatively the SAFEST of the four to eventually formalize into a semi-automated check, because the underlying question (does verified English text/audio support exist for this specific release?) is a checkable fact rather than a quality judgment -- but it still requires a per-title lookup, not an inference from region/publisher/genre, since many JP-region titles (fighters, shmups, racers, arcade, action) remain fully playable without language support.
